title: Campion and Duraeus amplify the calumny
source_text: II. Similiter Campianus, Rat. 8. de Protestantibus loquens, Docent, inquit, ne renatos quidem & sanctos quenquam esse aliud intrinsecus nisi meram corruptionem & contagionem. Et paulo post, Praeclaram isti partem assignant gratiae, quam neque in-fusam cordibus nostris, neque ad resistendum sceleribus validam esse latrant; sed extra nos in solo Dei favore collocant, qui favor non emendet impios, sed veterem istam sen-tinam adhuc manentem & foetentem, ne deformis & odiosa putetur, Deo connivente, dissimulet. Quibus audacius adhuc clamitans Duraeus, Minime miror, inquit, Cal-vinum nullam in nobis interioris hominis renovationem agnoscere, cum beatos ipsos sce-leribus suis, etiam in beatissimis illis sedibus, perpetuo esse contaminatos existimet. Rat. 8.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise Campion, Ratio 8, speaking of the Protestants, says they teach that even the regenerate and holy are inwardly nothing but mere corruption and contagion. And a little later: they assign a splendid share to grace, yet bark that it is neither infused into our hearts nor strong to resist crimes; they locate it only in God's favor outside us, which favor does not amend the wicked but, God conniving, dissembling, hides that old still-remaining and stinking bilge lest it seem deformed and odious. Duraeus clamors yet more boldly: he is not at all surprised that Calvin acknowledges no renovation of the inner man in us, since he judges the blessed themselves perpetually contaminated by their crimes even in those most blessed seats (Ratio 8).
pass_b_english: Campion: even the regenerate are mere corruption within; grace is only God's favor outside us.
Duraeus: Calvin denies interior renovation even of the blessed.
